--- title: "Model 1 extended: probability of payment with origin, registration status, CNAE division, size, instalments and protest" description: "How does the payment logit change when origin, register, activity, size, instalments and protest are added?" date: 2026-11-04 jupyter: python3 --- **Status:** exploration. Association only. This is not a forecast and not a rating. ::: {.callout-warning title="The register is later than the outcome"} Registration status, the activity division and size come from the register date printed by the setup cell. That date is after the payments. A coefficient on those fields is an association. It is not a prediction of a future payment, and a payment in the year is not recovery of the credit. ::: ::: {#setup .cell execution_count=1} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Source: VAT (ICMS) legal-entity extract, DuckDB read only. Window: 2016–2025. Rows after 2025 stay out of every table and every figure. Suppression: a cell with 1 to 4 distinct CNPJs is pooled as 'others (suppressed)'. A pool that still has fewer than 5 CNPJs is left blank. The count of pooled cells is printed with each table. Q1. Active = RFB code 02 (ATIVA). Inactive = codes 01, 03, 04, 08 (nula, suspensa, inapta, baixada). No establishment match, a root-only match, or any other code = unknown. Unknown is not forced into collectable or uncollectable. Q2. Payment history uses unit cnpj_root, scope vat_icms, denominator enrolled_value. The share is payments over enrolled value in the 5 calendar years that end in the reference year. The threshold is 10%. The unit's CDAs in the December snapshot enter the sum. The history is VAT (ICMS) only. Q3. Reference dates requested: 31 December of 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024. A year with no December snapshot is printed and left out of the tables. December 2024 is a partial snapshot because of a known gap in the DEBITO extract (EQ-05). Later recovery is the next calendar year, and the sum from the next year through 2025, each divided by the December stock. Q4. Precedence: suspended → guaranteed → instalment → unknown → active_history → inactive_history → active_recent → inactive_no_history → active_old. Suspended is uncollectable first. The guaranteed line is always emitted and is empty. no guarantee table in the data; collectable share is understated. Q5. Age bands (0, 2], (2, 5], (5, 10], >10. A value equal to a break stays in the lower band (left-closed is false). Ages from 0 to the first break are the first band. Both readings are shown: the annual paid/stock rate, and the cumulative recovery of cohorts enrolled in the window. The band above the last break is not observable on those cohorts. Q6. The outcome is any payment in the year, the same outcome as model 1 of the payment section. When the eligible frame is larger than 100,000 certificate-years, the fit uses a stratified sample of that size (year, origin, and the payment outcome), seed 2026. Standard errors are HC1. Clustered standard errors by CNPJ root are the column beside them. This is an association. It is not a forecast. Q7. One lab entry per block. Q8. The proposal material reports mean collection 1.38% against a collectable share 27.05%. The material states neither the year nor the tax cut. This page does not reproduce those two figures. It reports the analogous VAT (ICMS) legal-entity account. Registry attributes are the RFB extract 2026-03, which is later than the debts. CNAE enters as the division (two digits). ``` ::: ::: ## Question Holding the payment-section logit fixed, how do the associations change when origin, registration status, CNAE division, size, an earlier instalment and an earlier protest are added one block at a time? ## Data The sample is the one printed below: certificate-years with positive stock and an observed lag, inside the window. When that frame is larger than the cap printed by the setup cell, the fit draws a stratified sample of that size. The strata are the year, the origin and the payment outcome. The seed is the lab seed. The outcome is any payment in the year. The instalment flags use a request, or a valid break, dated before the year. The protest flag uses a protest date before the year, or records that the protest row has no date. The protest status itself is not a regressor. CNAE enters as the division. A division, a status or a size with fewer firms than the suppression floor is pooled. A pool that stays under the floor is dropped from every model, so the nested models share one sample. An origin, a registration status or a CNAE division with fewer than 10 payers in the sample is merged into `other` before the fit. If that pool still has fewer than 10 payers, those rows are left out, so a level with no payers is not a coefficient. ## Method Model 1 is the payment-section logit $$\Pr(\mathrm{paid\_flag}_{it}=1)=\Lambda(\beta_0+\beta_1\log\mathrm{stock}_{it}+\beta_2\mathrm{age}_{it}+\beta_3\mathrm{rate}_{i,t-1}+\gamma_{t})$$ $\Lambda$ is the logistic function. $\gamma_t$ is a year fixed effect. The odds ratio of a coefficient is $\exp(\hat\beta)$. The nested models add, in order, origin, registration status, CNAE division, size, the two instalment flags, and the dated protest flag. The likelihood is maximised with Newton (IRLS), the same solver as section 5.6.1. A fit that stops with a mean score above the tolerance, or with a pseudo-R² that is not positive, is rejected. Standard errors are HC1. The column beside them is the cluster-robust standard error by the firm root, computed from the same fit. Stars follow the lab rule printed below. McFadden's pseudo-R² is the value statsmodels reports as `prsquared`. AIC and BIC are the values on the fitted object. A second render reads the coefficient tables from the on-disk cache when the sample and the inputs are unchanged. The probability of non-recovery in the proposal equals one minus this fitted probability only when recovery means any payment in the year. That equivalence is not used as a rating here. ## How to read One row of the coefficient table is one term in one nested model. The odds ratio is the multiplicative change in the odds of a payment in the year when the term increases by one unit and the other terms stay fixed. An odds ratio above one is a positive association with payment. The confidence interval is the HC1 interval on the odds ratio. Stars mark the lab thresholds. They are not corrected for the number of tests. The fit table is one row per model. Read the pseudo-R², AIC and BIC as a comparison of nested associations on the same sample. A lower AIC is a better in-sample description. It is not an out-of-sample score. In the figure, the horizontal axis is the term of model 1 and the vertical axis is the odds ratio. The dotted line at one is no association. The figure omits the year fixed effects. They remain in the model. ::: {#tbl-fit .cell tbl-cap='Nested logits.
